html:
The Wappinger were a Munsee-speaking Native American people of the east bank of the lower Hudson River, in today's Dutchess, Putnam and Westchester counties of New York and parts of western Connecticut. They were a loose confederacy of bands, close to the Munsee Lenape across the river and to the Mahican to the north; Connecticut bands such as the Paugussett and Wangunk are sometimes counted with them.

They lived by farming maize, fishing and hunting, and traded furs with the Dutch of New Netherland after 1609. In Kieft's War of 1643 to 1645 the Dutch attacked them and their neighbours, and hundreds were killed.

Pushed off their land in the 1700s, many Wappinger joined the Mahican mission town of Stockbridge in Massachusetts. In the American Revolution their sachem Daniel Nimham fought for the Patriots and was killed in 1778. The survivors moved west with the Stockbridge-Munsee, who live in Wisconsin today.
